@graph.name: Port of New York and New Jersey Logistics Dataset
@graph.description: The per-port dataset for the Port of New York and New Jersey in the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the full port record for the largest container port on the U.S. East Coast and the third-largest in the nation — a landlord port owned by The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey (a bi-state authority established in 1921) and run by private terminal operators under long-term leases — its container terminals (Maher Terminals and APM Terminals Elizabeth at Elizabeth–Port Authority Marine Terminal; Port Newark Container Terminal at Port Newark; Port Liberty Bayonne at Port Jersey; Port Liberty New York at Howland Hook, Staten Island; Red Hook Container Terminal in Brooklyn), the Port Newark auto terminal (FAPS), its 50-foot harbor channel, its container volume on the Port Authority's named bases (8,897,531 TEU in CY2025; 8,698,526 TEU in CY2024), ExpressRail service by the two Class I partners CSX and Norfolk Southern with Conrail Shared Assets switching, the I-95 (New Jersey Turnpike), I-78, I-287 and US-1/9 corridors, Foreign-Trade Zone 49, and the branch binding: the port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch, about 251.1 road miles away (Winchester measures 275.6). The company's eight attached port services are recorded cell by cell in the companion coverage dataset. No port tenancy or port-authority relationship is claimed; the company's crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards.

@graph.name: Port of New York and New Jersey Service Coverage Dataset
@graph.description: The service-coverage cells for the Port of New York and New Jersey in the Ports & Intermodal program: the eight attached services (transloading; ocean container packing and unpacking; loading and unloading / container labor; cross-docking; freight rework; specialized workforce; logistics project management; 3PL support services), each recorded as offered with its delivery points (port-adjacent warehouse, receiver's dock, yard, leased space, and on-terminal by arrangement — on-terminal work happens only by arrangement through the terminal's own processes, never as a bare claim) and its bound branch, Martinsburg, WV. Drayage is not offered at any port in the program.

@graph.name: Port of New York and New Jersey
@graph.alternateName: Port of New York and New Jersey
@graph.description: Port of New York and New Jersey (Elizabeth, NJ) — deepwater marine port (containers, autos and RoRo, bulk, breakbulk) — the largest container port on the U.S. East Coast and the third-largest in the United States. Authority: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. Operator: Multiple private terminal operators running Port Authority terminals under long-term leases (landlord port — the Port Authority owns the terminals, the operators run them). Cargo: containers; autos and roll-on/roll-off vehicles; bulk (salt, cement, edible oils and juice, aggregates); breakbulk and project cargo. Rail: CSX — Class I partner serving the port through the ExpressRail system; Norfolk Southern — Class I partner serving the port through the ExpressRail system; Conrail Shared Assets Operations — switching carrier for CSX and Norfolk Southern in the North Jersey shared-assets district — not a third Class I. Highway corridors: I-95 (New Jersey Turnpike), I-78, I-287, US-1/9. Foreign-trade zone: FTZ 49, Newark/Elizabeth (grantee The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey). U.S. Customs port of entry. Volume (CY2025, calendar): 8,897,531 TEU — Port of New York and New Jersey system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ year-end 2025 release, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Volume (CY2024, calendar): 8,698,526 TEU — Port of New York and New Jersey system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ, Cargo Facility Charge Annual Report 2025, Table 2, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Volume (CY2024, calendar): 639,657 rail lifts (units) — ExpressRail system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ, Cargo Facility Charge Annual Report 2025, Table 2, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Volume (CY2024, calendar): 410,092 autos (units) — Port of New York and New Jersey system (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ, Port 2024 At A Glance, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Volume (CY2024, calendar): 2,785,839 metric tons — system total bulk tonnage (source: Port Authority of NY & NJ, Port 2024 At A Glance, via Port #8 research verification 2026-11-10). Branch binding: this port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 275.6 road miles from Winchester and 251.1 from Martinsburg; bound to Martinsburg on miles. about 24.5 mi closer from Martinsburg (OSRM road routing measured 2026-11-10 to the Elizabeth Marine Terminal point from both branches).
